hook: A cluttered garage full of tools to find: tap each object in the picture, then give it its article.
intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one lived-in home garage that doubles as a workshop, with 32 things to find in it — der Schraubstock on the workbench, die Zange on the pegboard, das Verlängerungskabel coiled on the floor. The prompt asks Wo ist der Rasenmäher? and you tap it in the picture. A tap on bare wall costs nothing; a tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking, and after three misses the right one is shown. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Rasenmäher?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself. No object is asked twice in the same run.
tips[0].title: Compounds in the garage: the last part decides
tips[0].text: Many tools are compounds, and the last part decides the article. Werkzeug + Kasten: der Kasten, so der Werkzeugkasten. Vorhänge + Schloss: das Schloss, so das Vorhängeschloss. Cover the front part and read only the last word.
tips[0].check.why: The last part is die Lampe, so the whole word is die Taschenlampe.
tips[1].title: -er makes a tool masculine — but not every -er word
tips[1].text: A machine or tool that does a job, named after its verb with -er, is masculine: der Rasenmäher (mähen), der Feuerlöscher (löschen), der Schraubenzieher (ziehen). An -er ending on its own proves nothing, though: die Leiter and das Fenster are in this garage too.
tips[1].check.why: Leiter is not a doer made from a verb; it is simply feminine: die Leiter.
tips[2].title: Many tools in -e are feminine
tips[2].text: Listen for the final -e: die Säge, die Zange, die Schubkarre, die Luftpumpe. Most two-syllable nouns ending in -e are die, so when a tool ends in -e, try die first and say it aloud with every find.
tips[2].check.why: Säge ends in -e, and like most such nouns it is feminine.
remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: das Schloss → das Vorhängeschloss.
remember[1]: Doers made from a verb with -er are der (der Rasenmäher), but die Leiter and das Fenster are not.
remember[2]: Tools ending in -e are usually die: die Säge, die Zange.
